questions.subject: Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question:
With reference to Fundamental Rights & Constitutional Remedies, consider the following three statements:
1. Article 32 guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and was described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the 'very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it'.
2. While the Supreme Court issues writs only for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights under Article 32, High Courts under Article 226 have wider writ jurisdiction extending to both Fundamental Rights and ordinary legal rights ('for any other purpose').
3. The writ jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 32 is wider than that of a High Court under Article 226 because it includes ordinary legal rights.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation:
Only two statements (Statements 1 and 2) are correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
• Statement 1 is correct: Article 32 guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and was described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the 'very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it'.
• Statement 2 is correct: While the Supreme Court issues writs only for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights under Article 32, High Courts under Article 226 have wider writ jurisdiction extending to both Fundamental Rights and ordinary legal rights ('for any other purpose').
• Statement 3 is incorrect: 'The writ jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 32 is wider than that of a High Court under Article 226 because it includes ordinary legal rights.' is a false statement.
• PYQ Pattern Note: The 'How many of the above statements are correct' format was extensively asked in the APPSC Group-I (2023 & 2024) and Group-II (Feb 2024) Prelims to eliminate guesswork.
questions.source: Constitution of India - Part III & Supreme Court Judgments (APPSC 2024 PYQ Pattern)

questions.question:

• Statement 2 is correct: This reservation also applies within the seats reserved for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs), and will take effect after the publication of the first Census and subsequent delimitation exercise following the Act's enactment, for a period of 15 years.

questions.question:

2. Lothal (on the Bhogavo river in Gujarat) featured an artificial brick tidal dockyard and bead-making factory, while Kalibangan (Rajasthan) provided evidence of the earliest ploughed agricultural field and fire altars.
3. Dholavira is located in the Gangetic plains of Bihar and lacked any drainage or water storage systems.

• Statement 2 is correct: Lothal (on the Bhogavo river in Gujarat) featured an artificial brick tidal dockyard and bead-making factory, while Kalibangan (Rajasthan) provided evidence of the earliest ploughed agricultural field and fire altars.
• Statement 3 is incorrect: 'Dholavira is located in the Gangetic plains of Bihar and lacked any drainage or water storage systems.' is a false statement.

questions.subject: AP History & Reorganization
questions.topic: Chronology of Andhra Maha Sabha & State Formation (APPSC PYQ)
questions.question:
Arrange the following milestones in the movement for a separate Andhra Province in correct chronological order from earliest to latest:
1. First Andhra Mahasabha Conference at Bapatla (presided over by B.N. Sarma)
2. Signing of the Sribagh Pact between Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema leaders
3. Appointment of the JVP Committee (Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel, Pattabhi Sitaramayya)
4. Martyrdom of Amarajeevi Potti Sreeramulu after 58 days of fast

Select the correct chronological code:
questions.explanation:
The correct chronological sequence is 1 - 2 - 3 - 4:
• 1. First Andhra Mahasabha Conference at Bapatla: May 1913 (presided over by Bayya Narasimheswara Sarma).
• 2. Sribagh Pact: November 16, 1937.
• 3. Dhar Commission & JVP Committee: December 1948 – April 1949.
• 4. Martyrdom of Potti Sreeramulu: December 15, 1952 (leading to the formation of Andhra State on October 1, 1953).
questions.source: APPSC Group-I Prelims (2023) & Group-II Mains (2019) Official PYQ

questions.subject: Indian History & National Movement
questions.topic: Buddhism & Jainism in Ancient India & Andhra (APPSC 2024 Prelims PYQ)
questions.question:
With reference to Buddhist sites and councils in Ancient India and Andhra Pradesh (asked in APPSC Group-I & Group-II Prelims 2024), consider the following statements:
1. The Mahachaitya at Amaravati (Dhanyakataka) was a major centre of the Mahasanghika (Chaityaka / Purvasaila) school of Buddhism.
2. Acharya Nagarjuna propounded the Madhyamika (Sunyavada) philosophy of Mahayana Buddhism and resided at Sriparvata (Nagarjunakonda).
3. The Fourth Buddhist Council was held at Kundalavana in Kashmir under the patronage of Kanishka and presided over by Vasumitra.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation:
Statements 1, 2 and 3 are all correct:
• Amaravati (Dhanyakataka) and Bhattiprolu were among the earliest and greatest centres of Buddhism in Andhra, strongly associated with the Mahasanghika sect (Chaityakas, Purvasailas, Aparasailas).
• Acharya Nagarjuna authored 'Mulamadhyamakakarika' and 'Suhrullekha', expounding Sunyavada (Madhyamika) at Sriparvata.
• Kanishka convened the 4th Buddhist Council in Kashmir with Vasumitra as President and Asvaghosha as Vice-President.
questions.source: APPSC Group-II Screening Test (Feb 2024) & Group-I Prelims (March 2024) Official PYQ

questions.subject: AP History & Reorganization
questions.topic: Nasik Inscription & Satavahanas (APPSC Group-II 2024 & Group-I PYQ)
questions.question:
Match List-I (Ancient Inscription in AP/Deccan) with List-II (Ruler/Issuer) as asked in APPSC Previous Year Papers:
List-I:
A. Nasik Prasasti
B. Nanaghat Inscription
C. Myakadoni Inscription
D. Motupalli Abhaya Sasana

List-II:
1. Naganika
2. Gautami Balasri
3. Pulumavi III (Last Satavahana king)
4. Ganapatideva (Kakatiya)

Select the correct code:
questions.explanation:
Correct Match is A-2, B-1, C-3, D-4.
• Nasik Prasasti was issued by Gautami Balasri praising the conquests of her son Gautamiputra Satakarni.
• Nanaghat Inscription was issued by Queen Naganika (wife of Satakarni I) describing Vedic sacrifices.
• Myakadoni Inscription (Bellary/Kurnool border) belongs to Pulumavi III, documenting the decline of the Satavahanas.
• Motupalli Abhaya Sasana (1244 CE) was issued by Kakatiya monarch Ganapatideva.
questions.source: APPSC Group-II Screening Test (Feb 2024) & Group-II Mains (2019) Official PYQ

questions.topic: Vijayanagara Foreign Travellers (APPSC Group-I & II PYQ)
questions.question:
Consider the following pairs of Foreign Travellers to the Vijayanagara Empire and the Rulers whose courts they visited:
1. Niccolo de' Conti — Devaraya I
2. Abdur Razzaq — Devaraya II
3. Domingo Paes — Sri Krishnadevaraya
4. Fernao Nuniz — Achyutadevaraya

How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.explanation:
All four pairs are correctly matched:
• Niccolo de' Conti (Italian) visited Vijayanagara around 1420 CE during the reign of Devaraya I.

options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct under Article 164(1A)

Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct

questions.topic: Rivers & Tributaries of Andhra Pradesh (APPSC Group-I & II 2024 PYQ)
questions.question:
Consider the following pairs of Rivers flowing through Andhra Pradesh and their Tributaries:
1. Godavari — Sabari and Indravati
2. Krishna — Tungabhadra, Musi and Munneru
3. Penna (Pennar) — Jayamangali, Kunderu, Sagileru, Chitravati and Papagni
4. Vamsadhara — Mahendratanaya

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation:
All four pairs (1, 2, 3 and 4) are correctly matched.
• Sabari (joining at Kunavaram) and Indravati are major left-bank tributaries of the Godavari.

• Mahendratanaya is a major tributary of the Vamsadhara river in Srikakulam/Parvathipuram Manyam region.

questions.question:
Match List-I (Five-Year Plan / Economic Policy) with List-II (Core Strategy / Growth Model) as tested in APPSC Group-I & Group-II Economy papers:
List-I:
A. First Five-Year Plan (1951–56)
B. Second Five-Year Plan (1956–61)
C. Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974–79)
D. Eleventh Five-Year Plan (2007–12)

List-II:
1. Harrod-Domar Model (Agriculture & Irrigation priority)
2. P.C. Mahalanobis Four-Sector Model (Rapid Heavy Industrialization)
3. D.D. Dhar Model ('Garibi Hatao' / Poverty Alleviation & Minimum Needs)
4. 'Faster and More Inclusive Growth'

Select the correct code:
questions.explanation:
Correct Match is A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4:
• First Plan (1951–56) was based on the Harrod-Domar growth model focusing on agriculture, price stability, and multipurpose river valley projects.
• Second Plan (1956–61) was architected by P.C. Mahalanobis emphasizing capital goods and heavy industries (Bhilai, Durgapur, Rourkela steel plants).
• Fifth Plan (1974–79) drafted by D.D. Dhar focused on poverty removal (Garibi Hatao) and self-reliance.
• Eleventh Plan (2007–12) had the theme 'Faster and More Inclusive Growth', followed by the Twelfth Plan ('Faster, More Inclusive and Sustainable Growth').

2. The Monetary Policy Committee consists of 10 members chaired by the Union Finance Secretary and targets Wholesale Price Index (WPI) inflation at 2%.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
• Statement 1 is correct: Under Section 45ZB of the amended RBI Act, 1934, the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is a six-member statutory body (3 from RBI including the Governor as ex-officio Chairperson, and 3 external members appointed by the Central Government) tasked with maintaining price stability while keeping in mind the objective of growth.
• Statement 2 is incorrect because: The flexible inflation targeting framework mandates maintaining Consumer Price Index (CPI-Combined) inflation at 4% with a tolerance band of +/- 2% (i.e., 2% to 6%). The RBI Governor holds a casting vote in case of a tie. (The claim that 'The Monetary Policy Committee consists of 10 members chaired by the Union Finance Secretary and targets Wholesale Price Index (WPI) inflation at 2%.' is factually false).

2. Dholavira is located in the Gangetic plains of Bihar and lacked any drainage or water storage systems.

questions.subject: Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question:
With reference to Centre-State Legislative Relations & Seventh Schedule, consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 249, Parliament is empowered to legislate on any matter in the State List in the national interest if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.
2. Under Article 249, only the Lok Sabha can authorize Parliament to legislate on a State List subject by a simple majority.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
• Statement 1 is correct: Under Article 249, Parliament is empowered to legislate on any matter in the State List in the national interest if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.
• Statement 2 is incorrect because: Such a resolution remains in force for one year at a time (renewable any number of times by one year each). Residuary powers of legislation are vested in the Union Parliament under Article 248. (The claim that 'Under Article 249, only the Lok Sabha can authorize Parliament to legislate on a State List subject by a simple majority.' is factually false).

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question:
Statements:
1. All Collectors are Civil Servants.
2. All Civil Servants are Public Authorities.
3. Some Public Authorities are Constitutional Functionaries.

Conclusions:
I. All Collectors are Public Authorities.
II. All Constitutional Functionaries are Collectors.

Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step Venn diagram analysis:
• Since All Collectors ⊂ Civil Servants and All Civil Servants ⊂ Public Authorities, by transitivity All Collectors are definitely Public Authorities (Conclusion I follows).
• Conclusion II does not follow because 'Some Public Authorities are Constitutional Functionaries' does not imply all of them are Collectors.

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: Under a Self-Help Group (SHG) linkage programme, Rs. 1,44,000 is distributed among three groups P, Q, and R in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. How much more amount does Group R receive than Group P?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Total ratio parts = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 parts.
• Value of 1 part = Rs. 1,44,000 / 12 = Rs. 12,000.
• Difference between Group R (5 parts) and Group P (3 parts) = 5 - 3 = 2 parts.
• Required difference = 2 × Rs. 12,000 = Rs. 24,000.

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: Engineer Team A can complete a section of the Polavaram feeder canal in 20 days, and Engineer Team B can complete the same section in 30 days. They work together for 8 days, after which Team A leaves. In how many days will Team B alone finish the remaining work?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• A's 1 day work = 1/20; B's 1 day work = 1/30.
• Combined 1 day work of (A + B) = 1/20 + 1/30 = (3 + 2)/60 = 5/60 = 1/12.
• Work done in 8 days together = 8 × (1/12) = 2/3.
• Remaining work = 1 - 2/3 = 1/3.
• Time taken by B alone to finish 1/3 work = (1/3) / (1/30) = 10 days.
questions.source: PYQ 02: APPSC Group-I Prelims (17 March 2024) Official Key & APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.topic: Rivers & Tributaries of Andhra Pradesh (APPSC Group-I & II 2024 PYQ)
questions.question:
Consider the following pairs of Rivers flowing through Andhra Pradesh and their Tributaries:
1. Godavari — Sabari and Indravati
2. Krishna — Tungabhadra, Musi and Munneru
3. Penna (Pennar) — Jayamangali, Kunderu, Sagileru, Chitravati and Papagni
4. Vamsadhara — Mahendratanaya

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation:
All four pairs (1, 2, 3 and 4) are correctly matched.
• Sabari (joining at Kunavaram) and Indravati are major left-bank tributaries of the Godavari.
• Tungabhadra, Bhima, Musi, and Munneru are key tributaries of the Krishna River.
• The Penna River (originating in Nandi Hills, Karnataka and draining into Bay of Bengal at Utukuru, Nellore) has Left-bank tributaries Jayamangali, Kunderu, and Sagileru, and Right-bank tributaries Chitravati, Papagni, and Cheyyeru.
• Mahendratanaya is a major tributary of the Vamsadhara river in Srikakulam/Parvathipuram Manyam region.

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: Engineer Team A can complete a section of the Polavaram feeder canal in 20 days, and Engineer Team B can complete the same section in 30 days. They work together for 8 days, after which Team A leaves. In how many days will Team B alone finish the remaining work?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• A's 1 day work = 1/20; B's 1 day work = 1/30.
• Combined 1 day work of (A + B) = 1/20 + 1/30 = (3 + 2)/60 = 5/60 = 1/12.
• Work done in 8 days together = 8 × (1/12) = 2/3.
• Remaining work = 1 - 2/3 = 1/3.
• Time taken by B alone to finish 1/3 work = (1/3) / (1/30) = 10 days.
questions.source: PYQ 03: APPSC Group-II Screening Test (25 Feb 2024) Official Key & APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.question: In a district development project in Andhra Pradesh, 40% of the total fund is allocated to irrigation, 25% of the remaining fund is allocated to rural roads, and the balance of Rs. 90 Crore is allocated to drinking water under Jal Jeevan Mission. What is the total project fund?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Let Total Fund = X.
• Irrigation allocation = 40% of X = 0.40X. Remaining fund = 60% of X = 0.60X.
• Rural roads = 25% of remaining (0.60X) = 0.25 × 0.60X = 0.15X.
• Balance left for drinking water = 0.60X - 0.15X = 0.45X.
• Given 0.45X = Rs. 90 Crore => X = 90 / 0.45 = Rs. 200 Crore.

questions.question:
Statements:

II. All Constitutional Functionaries are Collectors.

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: The average foodgrain production of 5 mandals in Krishna district is 420 tonnes. If a 6th mandal's production is included, the average increases to 450 tonnes. What is the production of the 6th mandal?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Total production of 5 mandals = 5 × 420 = 2,100 tonnes.
• Total production of 6 mandals = 6 × 450 = 2,700 tonnes.
• Production of 6th mandal = 2,700 - 2,100 = 600 tonnes.

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: A Vande Bharat Express train 240 meters long crosses a telegraph pole in 8 seconds. How long will it take to cross a railway bridge 660 meters long at the same uniform speed?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Speed of the train = Length of train / Time to cross pole = 240 m / 8 s = 30 m/s.
• Total distance to cross the bridge = Length of train + Length of bridge = 240 m + 660 m = 900 m.
• Time required = 900 m / 30 m/s = 30 seconds.
questions.source: PYQ 03: APPSC Group-II Screening Test (25 Feb 2024) Official Key & APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: Under a Self-Help Group (SHG) linkage programme, Rs. 1,44,000 is distributed among three groups P, Q, and R in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. How much more amount does Group R receive than Group P?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Total ratio parts = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 parts.
• Value of 1 part = Rs. 1,44,000 / 12 = Rs. 12,000.
• Difference between Group R (5 parts) and Group P (3 parts) = 5 - 3 = 2 parts.
• Required difference = 2 × Rs. 12,000 = Rs. 24,000.
questions.source: PYQ 03: APPSC Group-II Screening Test (25 Feb 2024) Official Key & APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.subject: Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question:
Consider the following two statements (asked in APPSC Group-I Prelims pattern):
Statement-I: The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 stipulated that the total number of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, in the Council of Ministers in a State shall NOT exceed 15% of the total number of members of the Legislative Assembly of that State.
Statement-II: The same Amendment also provided that the number of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, in a State shall NOT be less than 12.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct under Article 164(1A)
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
Neither Statement-I nor Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation:
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct.
• The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 inserted Clause (1A) in Article 164 of the Constitution.
• Under Article 164(1A), the strength of the State Council of Ministers (including the CM) cannot exceed 15% of the total strength of the State Legislative Assembly, and cannot be less than 12.

questions.topic: Rivers & Tributaries of Andhra Pradesh (APPSC Group-I & II 2024 PYQ)
questions.question:
Consider the following pairs of Rivers flowing through Andhra Pradesh and their Tributaries:
1. Godavari — Sabari and Indravati
2. Krishna — Tungabhadra, Musi and Munneru
3. Penna (Pennar) — Jayamangali, Kunderu, Sagileru, Chitravati and Papagni
4. Vamsadhara — Mahendratanaya

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation:
All four pairs (1, 2, 3 and 4) are correctly matched.
• Sabari (joining at Kunavaram) and Indravati are major left-bank tributaries of the Godavari.
• Tungabhadra, Bhima, Musi, and Munneru are key tributaries of the Krishna River.
• The Penna River (originating in Nandi Hills, Karnataka and draining into Bay of Bengal at Utukuru, Nellore) has Left-bank tributaries Jayamangali, Kunderu, and Sagileru, and Right-bank tributaries Chitravati, Papagni, and Cheyyeru.
• Mahendratanaya is a major tributary of the Vamsadhara river in Srikakulam/Parvathipuram Manyam region.

questions.question: Find the missing number in the APPSC analytical series: 7, 15, 31, 63, 127, ?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step pattern:

• 15 × 2 + 1 = 31
• 31 × 2 + 1 = 63
• 63 × 2 + 1 = 127
• 127 × 2 + 1 = 255.

questions.question:
Arrange the following milestones in the movement for a separate Andhra Province in correct chronological order from earliest to latest:

2. Signing of the Sribagh Pact between Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema leaders
3. Appointment of the JVP Committee (Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel, Pattabhi Sitaramayya)

B. Nanaghat Inscription
C. Myakadoni Inscription
D. Motupalli Abhaya Sasana

1. Naganika

questions.question:
Consider the following two statements (asked in APPSC Group-I Prelims pattern):
Statement-I: The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 stipulated that the total number of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, in the Council of Ministers in a State shall NOT exceed 15% of the total number of members of the Legislative Assembly of that State.
Statement-II: The same Amendment also provided that the number of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, in a State shall NOT be less than 12.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct under Article 164(1A)
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
Neither Statement-I nor Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation:
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct.
• The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 inserted Clause (1A) in Article 164 of the Constitution.

questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy
questions.topic: Five-Year Plans & Economic Reforms (APPSC Group-II Mains & Group-I PYQ)
questions.question:
Match List-I (Five-Year Plan / Economic Policy) with List-II (Core Strategy / Growth Model) as tested in APPSC Group-I & Group-II Economy papers:
List-I:
A. First Five-Year Plan (1951–56)
B. Second Five-Year Plan (1956–61)
C. Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974–79)
D. Eleventh Five-Year Plan (2007–12)

List-II:
1. Harrod-Domar Model (Agriculture & Irrigation priority)
2. P.C. Mahalanobis Four-Sector Model (Rapid Heavy Industrialization)
3. D.D. Dhar Model ('Garibi Hatao' / Poverty Alleviation & Minimum Needs)
4. 'Faster and More Inclusive Growth'

Select the correct code:
questions.explanation:
Correct Match is A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4:
• First Plan (1951–56) was based on the Harrod-Domar growth model focusing on agriculture, price stability, and multipurpose river valley projects.
• Second Plan (1956–61) was architected by P.C. Mahalanobis emphasizing capital goods and heavy industries (Bhilai, Durgapur, Rourkela steel plants).
• Fifth Plan (1974–79) drafted by D.D. Dhar focused on poverty removal (Garibi Hatao) and self-reliance.
• Eleventh Plan (2007–12) had the theme 'Faster and More Inclusive Growth', followed by the Twelfth Plan ('Faster, More Inclusive and Sustainable Growth').
questions.source: APPSC Group-II Mains Paper-III (2019) & Group-I Prelims (2023/2024) Official PYQ

questions.topic: Rivers & Tributaries of Andhra Pradesh (APPSC Group-I & II 2024 PYQ)
questions.question:
Consider the following pairs of Rivers flowing through Andhra Pradesh and their Tributaries:
1. Godavari — Sabari and Indravati
2. Krishna — Tungabhadra, Musi and Munneru
3. Penna (Pennar) — Jayamangali, Kunderu, Sagileru, Chitravati and Papagni
4. Vamsadhara — Mahendratanaya

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation:
All four pairs (1, 2, 3 and 4) are correctly matched.
• Sabari (joining at Kunavaram) and Indravati are major left-bank tributaries of the Godavari.
• Tungabhadra, Bhima, Musi, and Munneru are key tributaries of the Krishna River.
• The Penna River (originating in Nandi Hills, Karnataka and draining into Bay of Bengal at Utukuru, Nellore) has Left-bank tributaries Jayamangali, Kunderu, and Sagileru, and Right-bank tributaries Chitravati, Papagni, and Cheyyeru.
• Mahendratanaya is a major tributary of the Vamsadhara river in Srikakulam/Parvathipuram Manyam region.
questions.source: APPSC Group-II Screening Test (Feb 2024) & Group-I Prelims (2024) Official PYQ

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question:
Statements:
1. All Collectors are Civil Servants.
2. All Civil Servants are Public Authorities.
3. Some Public Authorities are Constitutional Functionaries.

Conclusions:
I. All Collectors are Public Authorities.
II. All Constitutional Functionaries are Collectors.

Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step Venn diagram analysis:
• Since All Collectors ⊂ Civil Servants and All Civil Servants ⊂ Public Authorities, by transitivity All Collectors are definitely Public Authorities (Conclusion I follows).
• Conclusion II does not follow because 'Some Public Authorities are Constitutional Functionaries' does not imply all of them are Collectors.

questions.question:
With reference to Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council, consider the following statements:
1. The GST Council is a constitutional body established under Article 279A (inserted by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016), chaired by the Union Finance Minister with State Finance/Taxation Ministers as members.
2. The GST Council is a non-statutory body chaired by the NITI Aayog Vice-Chairperson where the Union Government holds a 51% veto weightage.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
• Statement 1 is correct: The GST Council is a constitutional body established under Article 279A (inserted by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016), chaired by the Union Finance Minister with State Finance/Taxation Ministers as members.
• Statement 2 is incorrect because: Every decision of the GST Council requires a majority of not less than three-fourths (75%) of the weighted votes of the members present and voting, where the Central Government's vote has a weightage of one-third (33.33%) and all State Governments together have a weightage of two-thirds (66.67%). (The claim that 'The GST Council is a non-statutory body chaired by the NITI Aayog Vice-Chairperson where the Union Government holds a 51% veto weightage.' is factually false).

Assertion (A): Bipin Chandra Pal's tour of Coastal Andhra in April 1907 (visiting Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Kakinada, Rajahmundry, and Vijayawada) galvanized the Vandemataram Movement, with Chilakamarthi Lakshmi Narasimham spontaneously composing the famous Telugu verse 'Bharata Desamunati Paadi Aavu'.
Reason (R): The Rajahmundry College incident (1907) saw students suspended by Principal Mark Hunter for wearing Vandemataram badges, while the Kotappakonda incident (1909) saw Chinnapa Reddy executed.

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) provides valid contextual/explanatory support to (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is completely unrelated to the subject of (A)
questions.explanation:
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and closely linked under Vandemataram & Swadeshi Movement in Andhra.
• Bipin Chandra Pal's tour of Coastal Andhra in April 1907 (visiting Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Kakinada, Rajahmundry, and Vijayawada) galvanized the Vandemataram Movement, with Chilakamarthi Lakshmi Narasimham spontaneously composing the famous Telugu verse 'Bharata Desamunati Paadi Aavu'.
• The Rajahmundry College incident (1907) saw students suspended by Principal Mark Hunter for wearing Vandemataram badges, while the Kotappakonda incident (1909) saw Chinnapa Reddy executed.
questions.source: PYQ 05: APPSC Group-I Prelims (26 May 2019) Official Key & History of Freedom Movement in Andhra Pradesh - State Committee

questions.question:
Consider the following pairs of Rivers flowing through Andhra Pradesh and their Tributaries:
1. Godavari — Sabari and Indravati
2. Krishna — Tungabhadra, Musi and Munneru
3. Penna (Pennar) — Jayamangali, Kunderu, Sagileru, Chitravati and Papagni
4. Vamsadhara — Mahendratanaya

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation:
All four pairs (1, 2, 3 and 4) are correctly matched.
• Sabari (joining at Kunavaram) and Indravati are major left-bank tributaries of the Godavari.
• Tungabhadra, Bhima, Musi, and Munneru are key tributaries of the Krishna River.
• The Penna River (originating in Nandi Hills, Karnataka and draining into Bay of Bengal at Utukuru, Nellore) has Left-bank tributaries Jayamangali, Kunderu, and Sagileru, and Right-bank tributaries Chitravati, Papagni, and Cheyyeru.
• Mahendratanaya is a major tributary of the Vamsadhara river in Srikakulam/Parvathipuram Manyam region.

questions.topic: Five-Year Plans & Economic Reforms (APPSC Group-II Mains & Group-I PYQ)
questions.question:
Match List-I (Five-Year Plan / Economic Policy) with List-II (Core Strategy / Growth Model) as tested in APPSC Group-I & Group-II Economy papers:
List-I:
A. First Five-Year Plan (1951–56)
B. Second Five-Year Plan (1956–61)
C. Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974–79)
D. Eleventh Five-Year Plan (2007–12)

List-II:
1. Harrod-Domar Model (Agriculture & Irrigation priority)
2. P.C. Mahalanobis Four-Sector Model (Rapid Heavy Industrialization)
3. D.D. Dhar Model ('Garibi Hatao' / Poverty Alleviation & Minimum Needs)
4. 'Faster and More Inclusive Growth'

Select the correct code:
questions.explanation:
Correct Match is A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4:
• First Plan (1951–56) was based on the Harrod-Domar growth model focusing on agriculture, price stability, and multipurpose river valley projects.
• Second Plan (1956–61) was architected by P.C. Mahalanobis emphasizing capital goods and heavy industries (Bhilai, Durgapur, Rourkela steel plants).
• Fifth Plan (1974–79) drafted by D.D. Dhar focused on poverty removal (Garibi Hatao) and self-reliance.
• Eleventh Plan (2007–12) had the theme 'Faster and More Inclusive Growth', followed by the Twelfth Plan ('Faster, More Inclusive and Sustainable Growth').

Statement-II: The same Amendment also provided that the number of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, in a State shall NOT be less than 12.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct under Article 164(1A)
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
Neither Statement-I nor Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation:

questions.question:
With reference to Physical Geography of Andhra Pradesh & Coastline, consider the following statements:
1. Andhra Pradesh possesses the second-longest mainland coastline in India (~974 km) after Gujarat, stretching from Ichchapuram (Srikakulam district) in the north to Tada/Pulicat Lake (Tirupati district) in the south along the Bay of Bengal.
2. Andhra Pradesh has a landlocked border with no coastline, and Dodabetta is the highest mountain peak located in Guntur district.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
• Statement 1 is correct: Andhra Pradesh possesses the second-longest mainland coastline in India (~974 km) after Gujarat, stretching from Ichchapuram (Srikakulam district) in the north to Tada/Pulicat Lake (Tirupati district) in the south along the Bay of Bengal.
• Statement 2 is incorrect because: The Eastern Ghats in Andhra Pradesh are discontinuous, dissected by major east-flowing rivers (Godavari, Krishna, Penna, Nagavali, Vamsadhara). Jindhagada Peak (~1,690 m) in the Araku Valley / Alluri Sitharama Raju district is the highest peak in Andhra Pradesh. (The claim that 'Andhra Pradesh has a landlocked border with no coastline, and Dodabetta is the highest mountain peak located in Guntur district.' is factually false).

Match List-I (Ancient Inscription in AP/Deccan) with List-II (Ruler/Issuer) as asked in APPSC Previous Year Papers:
List-I:
A. Nasik Prasasti
B. Nanaghat Inscription
C. Myakadoni Inscription
D. Motupalli Abhaya Sasana

List-II:
1. Naganika
2. Gautami Balasri
3. Pulumavi III (Last Satavahana king)
4. Ganapatideva (Kakatiya)

Select the correct code:
questions.explanation:
Correct Match is A-2, B-1, C-3, D-4.
• Nasik Prasasti was issued by Gautami Balasri praising the conquests of her son Gautamiputra Satakarni.
• Nanaghat Inscription was issued by Queen Naganika (wife of Satakarni I) describing Vedic sacrifices.
• Myakadoni Inscription (Bellary/Kurnool border) belongs to Pulumavi III, documenting the decline of the Satavahanas.
• Motupalli Abhaya Sasana (1244 CE) was issued by Kakatiya monarch Ganapatideva.
questions.source: APPSC Group-II Screening Test (Feb 2024) & Group-II Mains (2019) Official PYQ

questions.topic: Chronology of Andhra Maha Sabha & State Formation (APPSC PYQ)
questions.question:
Arrange the following milestones in the movement for a separate Andhra Province in correct chronological order from earliest to latest:
1. First Andhra Mahasabha Conference at Bapatla (presided over by B.N. Sarma)
2. Signing of the Sribagh Pact between Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema leaders
3. Appointment of the JVP Committee (Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel, Pattabhi Sitaramayya)
4. Martyrdom of Amarajeevi Potti Sreeramulu after 58 days of fast

Select the correct chronological code:
questions.explanation:
The correct chronological sequence is 1 - 2 - 3 - 4:
• 1. First Andhra Mahasabha Conference at Bapatla: May 1913 (presided over by Bayya Narasimheswara Sarma).
• 2. Sribagh Pact: November 16, 1937.
• 3. Dhar Commission & JVP Committee: December 1948 – April 1949.
• 4. Martyrdom of Potti Sreeramulu: December 15, 1952 (leading to the formation of Andhra State on October 1, 1953).
questions.source: APPSC Group-I Prelims (2023) & Group-II Mains (2019) Official PYQ

questions.question:
Match List-I (Five-Year Plan / Economic Policy) with List-II (Core Strategy / Growth Model) as tested in APPSC Group-I & Group-II Economy papers:
List-I:
A. First Five-Year Plan (1951–56)
B. Second Five-Year Plan (1956–61)
C. Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974–79)
D. Eleventh Five-Year Plan (2007–12)

List-II:
1. Harrod-Domar Model (Agriculture & Irrigation priority)
2. P.C. Mahalanobis Four-Sector Model (Rapid Heavy Industrialization)

• Eleventh Plan (2007–12) had the theme 'Faster and More Inclusive Growth', followed by the Twelfth Plan ('Faster, More Inclusive and Sustainable Growth').

questions.question:
Consider the following pairs of Rivers flowing through Andhra Pradesh and their Tributaries:
1. Godavari — Sabari and Indravati
2. Krishna — Tungabhadra, Musi and Munneru
3. Penna (Pennar) — Jayamangali, Kunderu, Sagileru, Chitravati and Papagni
4. Vamsadhara — Mahendratanaya

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation:
All four pairs (1, 2, 3 and 4) are correctly matched.
• Sabari (joining at Kunavaram) and Indravati are major left-bank tributaries of the Godavari.
• Tungabhadra, Bhima, Musi, and Munneru are key tributaries of the Krishna River.
• The Penna River (originating in Nandi Hills, Karnataka and draining into Bay of Bengal at Utukuru, Nellore) has Left-bank tributaries Jayamangali, Kunderu, and Sagileru, and Right-bank tributaries Chitravati, Papagni, and Cheyyeru.
• Mahendratanaya is a major tributary of the Vamsadhara river in Srikakulam/Parvathipuram Manyam region.

With reference to Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM), consider the following statements:

2. Primary Deficit is calculated by adding Total Revenue Receipts to Gross Fiscal Deficit.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
• Statement 1 is correct: Primary Deficit is defined as Fiscal Deficit minus Interest Payments on previous borrowings, indicating the borrowing requirement of the government strictly for current year non-interest expenditure.
• Statement 2 is incorrect because: Effective Revenue Deficit (ERD) equals Revenue Deficit minus Grants-in-Aid for the creation of capital assets, distinguishing consumption expenditure from capital-building transfers to states. Under Section 45ZB of the amended RBI Act, 1934, the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is a six-member statutory body (3 from RBI including the Governor as ex-officio Chairperson, and 3 external members appointed by the Central Government) tasked with maintaining price stability while keeping in mind the objective of growth.
2. The Monetary Policy Committee consists of 10 members chaired by the Union Finance Secretary and targets Wholesale Price Index (WPI) inflation at 2%.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
• Statement 1 is correct: Under Section 45ZB of the amended RBI Act, 1934, the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is a six-member statutory body (3 from RBI including the Governor as ex-officio Chairperson, and 3 external members appointed by the Central Government) tasked with maintaining price stability while keeping in mind the objective of growth.

Furthermore, During the Northeast Monsoon, winds blowing over the warm Bay of Bengal pick up moisture and frequently interact with tropical cyclonic depressions to bring heavy post-monsoon rainfall to the Coromandel coast.
• Option (C) states 'Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema receive 100% of their rainfall only from Western Disturbances in January and zero rainfall from October to December.', which is false.

Only Statement 1 is correct.

questions.question: Find the missing number in the APPSC analytical series: 7, 15, 31, 63, 127, ?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step pattern:
• Each term follows the rule: (Previous Term × 2) + 1 (or 2^n - 1).

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: A Vande Bharat Express train 240 meters long crosses a telegraph pole in 8 seconds. How long will it take to cross a railway bridge 660 meters long at the same uniform speed?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Speed of the train = Length of train / Time to cross pole = 240 m / 8 s = 30 m/s.
• Total distance to cross the bridge = Length of train + Length of bridge = 240 m + 660 m = 900 m.
• Time required = 900 m / 30 m/s = 30 seconds.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: Under a Self-Help Group (SHG) linkage programme, Rs. 1,44,000 is distributed among three groups P, Q, and R in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. How much more amount does Group R receive than Group P?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Total ratio parts = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 parts.
• Value of 1 part = Rs. 1,44,000 / 12 = Rs. 12,000.
• Difference between Group R (5 parts) and Group P (3 parts) = 5 - 3 = 2 parts.
• Required difference = 2 × Rs. 12,000 = Rs. 24,000.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: Engineer Team A can complete a section of the Polavaram feeder canal in 20 days, and Engineer Team B can complete the same section in 30 days. They work together for 8 days, after which Team A leaves. In how many days will Team B alone finish the remaining work?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• A's 1 day work = 1/20; B's 1 day work = 1/30.
• Combined 1 day work of (A + B) = 1/20 + 1/30 = (3 + 2)/60 = 5/60 = 1/12.
• Work done in 8 days together = 8 × (1/12) = 2/3.
• Remaining work = 1 - 2/3 = 1/3.
• Time taken by B alone to finish 1/3 work = (1/3) / (1/30) = 10 days.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

2. While the Supreme Court issues writs only for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights under Article 32, High Courts under Article 226 have wider writ jurisdiction extending to both Fundamental Rights and ordinary legal rights ('for any other purpose').
3. The writ jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 32 is wider than that of a High Court under Article 226 because it includes ordinary legal rights.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation:
Only two statements (Statements 1 and 2) are correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
• Statement 1 is correct: Article 32 guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and was described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the 'very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it'.
• Statement 2 is correct: While the Supreme Court issues writs only for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights under Article 32, High Courts under Article 226 have wider writ jurisdiction extending to both Fundamental Rights and ordinary legal rights ('for any other purpose').
• Statement 3 is incorrect: 'The writ jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 32 is wider than that of a High Court under Article 226 because it includes ordinary legal rights.' is a false statement.

2. Under Article 249, only the Lok Sabha can authorize Parliament to legislate on a State List subject by a simple majority.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
• Statement 1 is correct: Under Article 249, Parliament is empowered to legislate on any matter in the State List in the national interest if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.

questions.explanation:

questions.subject: Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question: Which ONE of the following statements regarding Fundamental Rights & Constitutional Remedies is NOT correct?
options: Article 32 guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and was described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the 'very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it'.

While the Supreme Court issues writs only for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights under Article 32, High Courts under Article 226 have wider writ jurisdiction extending to both Fundamental Rights and ordinary legal rights ('for any other purpose').
The writ jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 32 is wider than that of a High Court under Article 226 because it includes ordinary legal rights.

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: Under a Self-Help Group (SHG) linkage programme, Rs. 1,44,000 is distributed among three groups P, Q, and R in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. How much more amount does Group R receive than Group P?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Total ratio parts = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 parts.
• Value of 1 part = Rs. 1,44,000 / 12 = Rs. 12,000.
• Difference between Group R (5 parts) and Group P (3 parts) = 5 - 3 = 2 parts.
• Required difference = 2 × Rs. 12,000 = Rs. 24,000.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: A Vande Bharat Express train 240 meters long crosses a telegraph pole in 8 seconds. How long will it take to cross a railway bridge 660 meters long at the same uniform speed?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Speed of the train = Length of train / Time to cross pole = 240 m / 8 s = 30 m/s.
• Total distance to cross the bridge = Length of train + Length of bridge = 240 m + 660 m = 900 m.
• Time required = 900 m / 30 m/s = 30 seconds.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.question: Find the missing number in the APPSC analytical series: 7, 15, 31, 63, 127, ?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step pattern:
• Each term follows the rule: (Previous Term × 2) + 1 (or 2^n - 1).

• 15 × 2 + 1 = 31
• 31 × 2 + 1 = 63
• 63 × 2 + 1 = 127
• 127 × 2 + 1 = 255.

questions.question:
Consider the following two statements (asked in APPSC Group-I Prelims pattern):
Statement-I: The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 stipulated that the total number of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, in the Council of Ministers in a State shall NOT exceed 15% of the total number of members of the Legislative Assembly of that State.
Statement-II: The same Amendment also provided that the number of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, in a State shall NOT be less than 12.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct under Article 164(1A)
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
Neither Statement-I nor Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation:
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct.
• The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 inserted Clause (1A) in Article 164 of the Constitution.
• Under Article 164(1A), the strength of the State Council of Ministers (including the CM) cannot exceed 15% of the total strength of the State Legislative Assembly, and cannot be less than 12.

questions.question:
Arrange the following milestones in the movement for a separate Andhra Province in correct chronological order from earliest to latest:
1. First Andhra Mahasabha Conference at Bapatla (presided over by B.N. Sarma)
2. Signing of the Sribagh Pact between Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema leaders
3. Appointment of the JVP Committee (Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel, Pattabhi Sitaramayya)
4. Martyrdom of Amarajeevi Potti Sreeramulu after 58 days of fast

questions.explanation:

questions.question:
Consider the following pairs of Rivers flowing through Andhra Pradesh and their Tributaries:
1. Godavari — Sabari and Indravati
2. Krishna — Tungabhadra, Musi and Munneru
3. Penna (Pennar) — Jayamangali, Kunderu, Sagileru, Chitravati and Papagni
4. Vamsadhara — Mahendratanaya

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation:
All four pairs (1, 2, 3 and 4) are correctly matched.
• Sabari (joining at Kunavaram) and Indravati are major left-bank tributaries of the Godavari.
• Tungabhadra, Bhima, Musi, and Munneru are key tributaries of the Krishna River.
• The Penna River (originating in Nandi Hills, Karnataka and draining into Bay of Bengal at Utukuru, Nellore) has Left-bank tributaries Jayamangali, Kunderu, and Sagileru, and Right-bank tributaries Chitravati, Papagni, and Cheyyeru.
• Mahendratanaya is a major tributary of the Vamsadhara river in Srikakulam/Parvathipuram Manyam region.
questions.source: APPSC Group-II Screening Test (Feb 2024) & Group-I Prelims (2024) Official PYQ

Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R) regarding Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM):

Assertion (A): Primary Deficit is defined as Fiscal Deficit minus Interest Payments on previous borrowings, indicating the borrowing requirement of the government strictly for current year non-interest expenditure.
Reason (R): Effective Revenue Deficit (ERD) equals Revenue Deficit minus Grants-in-Aid for the creation of capital assets, distinguishing consumption expenditure from capital-building transfers to states.

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) provides valid contextual/explanatory support to (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is completely unrelated to the subject of (A)
questions.explanation:
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and closely linked under Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM).
• Primary Deficit is defined as Fiscal Deficit minus Interest Payments on previous borrowings, indicating the borrowing requirement of the government strictly for current year non-interest expenditure.
• Effective Revenue Deficit (ERD) equals Revenue Deficit minus Grants-in-Aid for the creation of capital assets, distinguishing consumption expenditure from capital-building transfers to states.
questions.source: Union Budget Documents & Ministry of Finance Glossary

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question:
Statements:
1. All Collectors are Civil Servants.
2. All Civil Servants are Public Authorities.
3. Some Public Authorities are Constitutional Functionaries.

Conclusions:
I. All Collectors are Public Authorities.
II. All Constitutional Functionaries are Collectors.

Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step Venn diagram analysis:
• Since All Collectors ⊂ Civil Servants and All Civil Servants ⊂ Public Authorities, by transitivity All Collectors are definitely Public Authorities (Conclusion I follows).
• Conclusion II does not follow because 'Some Public Authorities are Constitutional Functionaries' does not imply all of them are Collectors.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: The average foodgrain production of 5 mandals in Krishna district is 420 tonnes. If a 6th mandal's production is included, the average increases to 450 tonnes. What is the production of the 6th mandal?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Total production of 5 mandals = 5 × 420 = 2,100 tonnes.
• Total production of 6 mandals = 6 × 450 = 2,700 tonnes.
• Production of 6th mandal = 2,700 - 2,100 = 600 tonnes.

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: Engineer Team A can complete a section of the Polavaram feeder canal in 20 days, and Engineer Team B can complete the same section in 30 days. They work together for 8 days, after which Team A leaves. In how many days will Team B alone finish the remaining work?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• A's 1 day work = 1/20; B's 1 day work = 1/30.
• Combined 1 day work of (A + B) = 1/20 + 1/30 = (3 + 2)/60 = 5/60 = 1/12.
• Work done in 8 days together = 8 × (1/12) = 2/3.
• Remaining work = 1 - 2/3 = 1/3.
• Time taken by B alone to finish 1/3 work = (1/3) / (1/30) = 10 days.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: Under a Self-Help Group (SHG) linkage programme, Rs. 1,44,000 is distributed among three groups P, Q, and R in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. How much more amount does Group R receive than Group P?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Total ratio parts = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 parts.
• Value of 1 part = Rs. 1,44,000 / 12 = Rs. 12,000.
• Difference between Group R (5 parts) and Group P (3 parts) = 5 - 3 = 2 parts.
• Required difference = 2 × Rs. 12,000 = Rs. 24,000.

questions.question:
With reference to Biotechnology: CRISPR-Cas9, CAR-T Cell Therapy & Vaccines, consider the following statements:
1. NexCAR19, developed indigenously at IIT Bombay and Tata Memorial Centre and approved by CDSCO, is India's first indigenous Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-cell (CAR-T) gene therapy for treating relapsed/refractory B-cell lymphomas and leukemia at a fraction of global costs.
2. CAR-T cell therapy is an antibiotic ointment derived from marine algae used only for bacterial skin infections.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
• Statement 1 is correct: NexCAR19, developed indigenously at IIT Bombay and Tata Memorial Centre and approved by CDSCO, is India's first indigenous Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-cell (CAR-T) gene therapy for treating relapsed/refractory B-cell lymphomas and leukemia at a fraction of global costs.
• Statement 2 is incorrect because: Meanwhile, CRISPR-Cas9 (using guide RNA and Cas9 endonuclease) has enabled breakthroughs such as indigenous gene-editing research for Sickle Cell Anaemia under the National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission (targeting elimination by 2047). (The claim that 'CAR-T cell therapy is an antibiotic ointment derived from marine algae used only for bacterial skin infections.' is factually false).
questions.source: PIB - Department of Biotechnology (DBT) & Ministry of Health

questions.question:
With reference to ISRO Space Missions (Chandrayaan-3, Aditya-L1 & Gaganyaan), consider the following statements:
1. ISRO's Chandrayaan-3 successfully soft-landed its Vikram Lander (carrying the Pragyan Rover) near the lunar south pole (at ~69.37° S latitude, named 'Statio Shiv Shakti') on August 23, 2023—celebrated annually as 'National Space Day'—making India the first country to land near the lunar south pole and fourth overall to soft-land on the Moon.
2. Chandrayaan-3 landed on Mars' north pole using a GSLV Mk-I rocket, while Aditya-L1 orbits around Lagrange Point L3 behind the Sun.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
• Statement 1 is correct: ISRO's Chandrayaan-3 successfully soft-landed its Vikram Lander (carrying the Pragyan Rover) near the lunar south pole (at ~69.37° S latitude, named 'Statio Shiv Shakti') on August 23, 2023—celebrated annually as 'National Space Day'—making India the first country to land near the lunar south pole and fourth overall to soft-land on the Moon.
• Statement 2 is incorrect because: Subsequently, Aditya-L1 (launched via PSLV-C57 on September 2, 2023) was inserted into a halo orbit around the Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 1 (L1, ~1.5 million km from Earth) with 7 payloads (including VELC and SUIT) for continuous uninterrupted solar observation. (The claim that 'Chandrayaan-3 landed on Mars' north pole using a GSLV Mk-I rocket, while Aditya-L1 orbits around Lagrange Point L3 behind the Sun.' is factually false).
questions.source: PIB - Department of Space / ISRO Official Releases

questions.explanation:

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: Under a Self-Help Group (SHG) linkage programme, Rs. 1,44,000 is distributed among three groups P, Q, and R in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. How much more amount does Group R receive than Group P?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Total ratio parts = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 parts.
• Value of 1 part = Rs. 1,44,000 / 12 = Rs. 12,000.
• Difference between Group R (5 parts) and Group P (3 parts) = 5 - 3 = 2 parts.
• Required difference = 2 × Rs. 12,000 = Rs. 24,000.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

2. The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act reserves 33% seats for women in the Rajya Sabha and State Legislative Councils with immediate effect from 2024 without requiring delimitation.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
• Statement 1 is correct: The Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023 reserves one-third (33%) of all seats for women in the Lok Sabha (Article 330A), State Legislative Assemblies (Article 332A), and the Legislative Assembly of NCT of Delhi (Article 239AA).

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: A Vande Bharat Express train 240 meters long crosses a telegraph pole in 8 seconds. How long will it take to cross a railway bridge 660 meters long at the same uniform speed?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Speed of the train = Length of train / Time to cross pole = 240 m / 8 s = 30 m/s.
• Total distance to cross the bridge = Length of train + Length of bridge = 240 m + 660 m = 900 m.
• Time required = 900 m / 30 m/s = 30 seconds.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.question: The average foodgrain production of 5 mandals in Krishna district is 420 tonnes. If a 6th mandal's production is included, the average increases to 450 tonnes. What is the production of the 6th mandal?

questions.question: Under a Self-Help Group (SHG) linkage programme, Rs. 1,44,000 is distributed among three groups P, Q, and R in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. How much more amount does Group R receive than Group P?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Total ratio parts = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 parts.
• Value of 1 part = Rs. 1,44,000 / 12 = Rs. 12,000.
• Difference between Group R (5 parts) and Group P (3 parts) = 5 - 3 = 2 parts.
• Required difference = 2 × Rs. 12,000 = Rs. 24,000.

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: Engineer Team A can complete a section of the Polavaram feeder canal in 20 days, and Engineer Team B can complete the same section in 30 days. They work together for 8 days, after which Team A leaves. In how many days will Team B alone finish the remaining work?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• A's 1 day work = 1/20; B's 1 day work = 1/30.
• Combined 1 day work of (A + B) = 1/20 + 1/30 = (3 + 2)/60 = 5/60 = 1/12.
• Work done in 8 days together = 8 × (1/12) = 2/3.
• Remaining work = 1 - 2/3 = 1/3.
• Time taken by B alone to finish 1/3 work = (1/3) / (1/30) = 10 days.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) provides valid contextual/explanatory support to (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is completely unrelated to the subject of (A)
questions.explanation:

• The Mangampeta deposit in Annamayya/YSR Kadapa district of Andhra Pradesh holds the single largest reserve of Barytes in the world (accounting for over 90% of India's barytes resources), while the Tummalapalle belt is one of the largest strata-bound Uranium reserves globally.

questions.question:

questions.question:

3. Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve is the smallest wildlife sanctuary in India and is located in the Western Ghats of Kerala.

How many of the statements given above are correct?

Only two statements (Statements 1 and 2) are correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.

• Statement 2 is correct: The Seshachalam Hills (Tirupati/Annamayya/Kadapa districts) are designated as a Biosphere Reserve by MoEFCC and are the globally endemic habitat of the precious Red Sanders (Pterocarpus santalinus) and the Golden Gecko.

questions.subject: Indian History & National Movement
questions.topic: Buddhism & Jainism in Ancient India & Andhra (APPSC 2024 Prelims PYQ)
questions.question:
With reference to Buddhist sites and councils in Ancient India and Andhra Pradesh (asked in APPSC Group-I & Group-II Prelims 2024), consider the following statements:
1. The Mahachaitya at Amaravati (Dhanyakataka) was a major centre of the Mahasanghika (Chaityaka / Purvasaila) school of Buddhism.
2. Acharya Nagarjuna propounded the Madhyamika (Sunyavada) philosophy of Mahayana Buddhism and resided at Sriparvata (Nagarjunakonda).
3. The Fourth Buddhist Council was held at Kundalavana in Kashmir under the patronage of Kanishka and presided over by Vasumitra.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation:
Statements 1, 2 and 3 are all correct:
• Amaravati (Dhanyakataka) and Bhattiprolu were among the earliest and greatest centres of Buddhism in Andhra, strongly associated with the Mahasanghika sect (Chaityakas, Purvasailas, Aparasailas).
• Acharya Nagarjuna authored 'Mulamadhyamakakarika' and 'Suhrullekha', expounding Sunyavada (Madhyamika) at Sriparvata.
• Kanishka convened the 4th Buddhist Council in Kashmir with Vasumitra as President and Asvaghosha as Vice-President.
questions.source: APPSC Group-II Screening Test (Feb 2024) & Group-I Prelims (March 2024) Official PYQ

questions.topic: Kinship, Marriage & Family Systems in India
questions.question:
With reference to Kinship, Marriage & Family Systems in India, consider the following statements:
1. In Indian kinship sociology (analyzed by Irawati Karve in 'Kinship Organization in India'), Northern Indian kinship is strongly patrilineal with village exogamy and prohibition of cross-cousin marriages, whereas Dravidian (Southern Indian) kinship traditionally permits preferential cross-cousin and uncle-niece alliances while maintaining clan (gotra/intiperu) exogamy.
2. According to Irawati Karve, Southern Indian Dravidian kinship strictly prohibits all forms of cross-cousin marriage while Northern India practices matrilineal inheritance.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
• Statement 1 is correct: In Indian kinship sociology (analyzed by Irawati Karve in 'Kinship Organization in India'), Northern Indian kinship is strongly patrilineal with village exogamy and prohibition of cross-cousin marriages, whereas Dravidian (Southern Indian) kinship traditionally permits preferential cross-cousin and uncle-niece alliances while maintaining clan (gotra/intiperu) exogamy.
• Statement 2 is incorrect because: Meanwhile, matrilineal kinship systems have historically been practiced among the Khasis, Jaintias, and Garos of Meghalaya and the Nairs of Kerala (taravad system). (The claim that 'According to Irawati Karve, Southern Indian Dravidian kinship strictly prohibits all forms of cross-cousin marriage while Northern India practices matrilineal inheritance.' is factually false).
questions.source: APPSC Group 2 Indian Society Syllabus - Family, Marriage & Kinship

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: A Vande Bharat Express train 240 meters long crosses a telegraph pole in 8 seconds. How long will it take to cross a railway bridge 660 meters long at the same uniform speed?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Speed of the train = Length of train / Time to cross pole = 240 m / 8 s = 30 m/s.
• Total distance to cross the bridge = Length of train + Length of bridge = 240 m + 660 m = 900 m.
• Time required = 900 m / 30 m/s = 30 seconds.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: Under a Self-Help Group (SHG) linkage programme, Rs. 1,44,000 is distributed among three groups P, Q, and R in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. How much more amount does Group R receive than Group P?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Total ratio parts = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 parts.
• Value of 1 part = Rs. 1,44,000 / 12 = Rs. 12,000.
• Difference between Group R (5 parts) and Group P (3 parts) = 5 - 3 = 2 parts.
• Required difference = 2 × Rs. 12,000 = Rs. 24,000.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.topic: Rivers & Tributaries of Andhra Pradesh (APPSC Group-I & II 2024 PYQ)
questions.question:
Consider the following pairs of Rivers flowing through Andhra Pradesh and their Tributaries:
1. Godavari — Sabari and Indravati
2. Krishna — Tungabhadra, Musi and Munneru
3. Penna (Pennar) — Jayamangali, Kunderu, Sagileru, Chitravati and Papagni
4. Vamsadhara — Mahendratanaya

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation:
All four pairs (1, 2, 3 and 4) are correctly matched.
• Sabari (joining at Kunavaram) and Indravati are major left-bank tributaries of the Godavari.
• Tungabhadra, Bhima, Musi, and Munneru are key tributaries of the Krishna River.
• The Penna River (originating in Nandi Hills, Karnataka and draining into Bay of Bengal at Utukuru, Nellore) has Left-bank tributaries Jayamangali, Kunderu, and Sagileru, and Right-bank tributaries Chitravati, Papagni, and Cheyyeru.
• Mahendratanaya is a major tributary of the Vamsadhara river in Srikakulam/Parvathipuram Manyam region.
questions.source: APPSC Group-II Screening Test (Feb 2024) & Group-I Prelims (2024) Official PYQ

Which of the statements given above are correct?

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: A Vande Bharat Express train 240 meters long crosses a telegraph pole in 8 seconds. How long will it take to cross a railway bridge 660 meters long at the same uniform speed?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Speed of the train = Length of train / Time to cross pole = 240 m / 8 s = 30 m/s.
• Total distance to cross the bridge = Length of train + Length of bridge = 240 m + 660 m = 900 m.
• Time required = 900 m / 30 m/s = 30 seconds.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.explanation:

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: A Vande Bharat Express train 240 meters long crosses a telegraph pole in 8 seconds. How long will it take to cross a railway bridge 660 meters long at the same uniform speed?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Speed of the train = Length of train / Time to cross pole = 240 m / 8 s = 30 m/s.
• Total distance to cross the bridge = Length of train + Length of bridge = 240 m + 660 m = 900 m.
• Time required = 900 m / 30 m/s = 30 seconds.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.question: The average foodgrain production of 5 mandals in Krishna district is 420 tonnes. If a 6th mandal's production is included, the average increases to 450 tonnes. What is the production of the 6th mandal?

questions.question:
Statements:
1. All Collectors are Civil Servants.
2. All Civil Servants are Public Authorities.
3. Some Public Authorities are Constitutional Functionaries.

Conclusions:
I. All Collectors are Public Authorities.
II. All Constitutional Functionaries are Collectors.

Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.explanation:

• Since All Collectors ⊂ Civil Servants and All Civil Servants ⊂ Public Authorities, by transitivity All Collectors are definitely Public Authorities (Conclusion I follows).

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: Under a Self-Help Group (SHG) linkage programme, Rs. 1,44,000 is distributed among three groups P, Q, and R in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. How much more amount does Group R receive than Group P?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Total ratio parts = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 parts.
• Value of 1 part = Rs. 1,44,000 / 12 = Rs. 12,000.
• Difference between Group R (5 parts) and Group P (3 parts) = 5 - 3 = 2 parts.
• Required difference = 2 × Rs. 12,000 = Rs. 24,000.

questions.question: In a district development project in Andhra Pradesh, 40% of the total fund is allocated to irrigation, 25% of the remaining fund is allocated to rural roads, and the balance of Rs. 90 Crore is allocated to drinking water under Jal Jeevan Mission. What is the total project fund?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Let Total Fund = X.
• Irrigation allocation = 40% of X = 0.40X. Remaining fund = 60% of X = 0.60X.
• Rural roads = 25% of remaining (0.60X) = 0.25 × 0.60X = 0.15X.
• Balance left for drinking water = 0.60X - 0.15X = 0.45X.
• Given 0.45X = Rs. 90 Crore => X = 90 / 0.45 = Rs. 200 Crore.

• Correct facts: The Government of India Act, 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) introduced 'Dyarchy' in the Provinces (dividing provincial subjects into 'Transferred' and 'Reserved') and bicameralism at the Centre, whereas the Government of India Act, 1935 abolished Provincial Dyarchy, introduced 'Provincial Autonomy', and proposed an All-India Federation with a three-fold division of legislative lists (Federal, Provincial, Concurrent). Furthermore, The Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) had earlier introduced separate communal electorates for Muslims and brought Satyendra Prasad Sinha as the first Indian member into the Viceroy's Executive Council.
• Option (C) states 'The Government of India Act, 1935 introduced Provincial Dyarchy for the first time and abolished the Federal Court and Reserve Bank of India.', which is false.

questions.question:
Statements:

2. All Civil Servants are Public Authorities.
3. Some Public Authorities are Constitutional Functionaries.

Conclusions:
I. All Collectors are Public Authorities.
II. All Constitutional Functionaries are Collectors.

Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.explanation:

• Statement 2 is correct: The Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) had earlier introduced separate communal electorates for Muslims and brought Satyendra Prasad Sinha as the first Indian member into the Viceroy's Executive Council.

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: In a district development project in Andhra Pradesh, 40% of the total fund is allocated to irrigation, 25% of the remaining fund is allocated to rural roads, and the balance of Rs. 90 Crore is allocated to drinking water under Jal Jeevan Mission. What is the total project fund?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Let Total Fund = X.
• Irrigation allocation = 40% of X = 0.40X. Remaining fund = 60% of X = 0.60X.
• Rural roads = 25% of remaining (0.60X) = 0.25 × 0.60X = 0.15X.
• Balance left for drinking water = 0.60X - 0.15X = 0.45X.
• Given 0.45X = Rs. 90 Crore => X = 90 / 0.45 = Rs. 200 Crore.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

With reference to Kinship, Marriage & Family Systems in India, consider the following statements:
1. questions.question: The average foodgrain production of 5 mandals in Krishna district is 420 tonnes. If a 6th mandal's production is included, the average increases to 450 tonnes. What is the production of the 6th mandal?

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Constitutional & Statutory Safeguards for SCs, STs & OBCs:
1. questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: A Vande Bharat Express train 240 meters long crosses a telegraph pole in 8 seconds. How long will it take to cross a railway bridge 660 meters long at the same uniform speed?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Speed of the train = Length of train / Time to cross pole = 240 m / 8 s = 30 m/s.
• Total distance to cross the bridge = Length of train + Length of bridge = 240 m + 660 m = 900 m.
• Time required = 900 m / 30 m/s = 30 seconds.

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: Under a Self-Help Group (SHG) linkage programme, Rs. 1,44,000 is distributed among three groups P, Q, and R in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. How much more amount does Group R receive than Group P?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Total ratio parts = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 parts.
• Value of 1 part = Rs. 1,44,000 / 12 = Rs. 12,000.
• Difference between Group R (5 parts) and Group P (3 parts) = 5 - 3 = 2 parts.
• Required difference = 2 × Rs. 12,000 = Rs. 24,000.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.question:
With reference to Fundamental Rights & Constitutional Remedies, consider the following statements:
1. Article 32 guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and was described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the 'very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it'.
2. The writ jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 32 is wider than that of a High Court under Article 226 because it includes ordinary legal rights.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
• Statement 1 is correct: Article 32 guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and was described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the 'very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it'.
• Statement 2 is incorrect because: While the Supreme Court issues writs only for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights under Article 32, High Courts under Article 226 have wider writ jurisdiction extending to both Fundamental Rights and ordinary legal rights ('for any other purpose'). (The claim that 'The writ jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 32 is wider than that of a High Court under Article 226 because it includes ordinary legal rights.' is factually false).

questions.question:
With reference to Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) & RBI, consider the following statements:
1. Under Section 45ZB of the amended RBI Act, 1934, the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is a six-member statutory body (3 from RBI including the Governor as ex-officio Chairperson, and 3 external members appointed by the Central Government) tasked with maintaining price stability while keeping in mind the objective of growth.
2. The Monetary Policy Committee consists of 10 members chaired by the Union Finance Secretary and targets Wholesale Price Index (WPI) inflation at 2%.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
• Statement 1 is correct: Under Section 45ZB of the amended RBI Act, 1934, the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is a six-member statutory body (3 from RBI including the Governor as ex-officio Chairperson, and 3 external members appointed by the Central Government) tasked with maintaining price stability while keeping in mind the objective of growth.
• Statement 2 is incorrect because: The flexible inflation targeting framework mandates maintaining Consumer Price Index (CPI-Combined) inflation at 4% with a tolerance band of +/- 2% (i.e., 2% to 6%). The RBI Governor holds a casting vote in case of a tie. (The claim that 'The Monetary Policy Committee consists of 10 members chaired by the Union Finance Secretary and targets Wholesale Price Index (WPI) inflation at 2%.' is factually false).
questions.source: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Official Portal & PIB Finance Releases

questions.question:
Match List-I (Five-Year Plan / Economic Policy) with List-II (Core Strategy / Growth Model) as tested in APPSC Group-I & Group-II Economy papers:
List-I:
A. First Five-Year Plan (1951–56)
B. Second Five-Year Plan (1956–61)
C. Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974–79)
D. Eleventh Five-Year Plan (2007–12)

List-II:
1. Harrod-Domar Model (Agriculture & Irrigation priority)
2. P.C. Mahalanobis Four-Sector Model (Rapid Heavy Industrialization)
3. D.D. Dhar Model ('Garibi Hatao' / Poverty Alleviation & Minimum Needs)
4. 'Faster and More Inclusive Growth'

Select the correct code:
questions.explanation:
Correct Match is A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4:
• First Plan (1951–56) was based on the Harrod-Domar growth model focusing on agriculture, price stability, and multipurpose river valley projects.
• Second Plan (1956–61) was architected by P.C. Mahalanobis emphasizing capital goods and heavy industries (Bhilai, Durgapur, Rourkela steel plants).
• Fifth Plan (1974–79) drafted by D.D. Dhar focused on poverty removal (Garibi Hatao) and self-reliance.
• Eleventh Plan (2007–12) had the theme 'Faster and More Inclusive Growth', followed by the Twelfth Plan ('Faster, More Inclusive and Sustainable Growth').

Every decision of the GST Council requires a majority of not less than three-fourths (75%) of the weighted votes of the members present and voting, where the Central Government's vote has a weightage of one-third (33.33%) and all State Governments together have a weightage of two-thirds (66.67%).
The GST Council is a non-statutory body chaired by the NITI Aayog Vice-Chairperson where the Union Government holds a 51% veto weightage.
Official records under GST Council Secretariat & PIB Ministry of Finance document key provisions on Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council.
questions.explanation:
Option (C) is NOT correct.
• Correct facts: The GST Council is a constitutional body established under Article 279A (inserted by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016), chaired by the Union Finance Minister with State Finance/Taxation Ministers as members. Furthermore, Every decision of the GST Council requires a majority of not less than three-fourths (75%) of the weighted votes of the members present and voting, where the Central Government's vote has a weightage of one-third (33.33%) and all State Governments together have a weightage of two-thirds (66.67%).
• Option (C) states 'The GST Council is a non-statutory body chaired by the NITI Aayog Vice-Chairperson where the Union Government holds a 51% veto weightage.', which is false.
questions.source: GST Council Secretariat & PIB Ministry of Finance

questions.subject: Science, Tech & Environment
questions.question:
With reference to NISAR & Next-Generation Launch Vehicles (ISRO), consider the following statements:
1. NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar) is a joint Earth-observing satellite mission featuring dual-frequency radar: an L-band SAR provided by NASA and an S-band SAR provided by ISRO, using SweepSAR technology to map global land surface changes, ice-sheet dynamics, and natural hazards every 12 days.
2. NISAR is a deep-space telescope jointly built by Roscosmos and ESA without any radar payloads.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
• Statement 1 is correct: NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar) is a joint Earth-observing satellite mission featuring dual-frequency radar: an L-band SAR provided by NASA and an S-band SAR provided by ISRO, using SweepSAR technology to map global land surface changes, ice-sheet dynamics, and natural hazards every 12 days.
• Statement 2 is incorrect because: ISRO launches satellites primarily from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR) at Sriharikota in Tirupati district, Andhra Pradesh, utilizing PSLV, GSLV, LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark-3), and SSLV (Small Satellite Launch Vehicle). (The claim that 'NISAR is a deep-space telescope jointly built by Roscosmos and ESA without any radar payloads.' is factually false).
questions.source: ISRO Official Portal & PIB Science & Technology

With reference to Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM), consider the following statements:
1. Primary Deficit is defined as Fiscal Deficit minus Interest Payments on previous borrowings, indicating the borrowing requirement of the government strictly for current year non-interest expenditure.
2. Primary Deficit is calculated by adding Total Revenue Receipts to Gross Fiscal Deficit.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
• Statement 1 is correct: Primary Deficit is defined as Fiscal Deficit minus Interest Payments on previous borrowings, indicating the borrowing requirement of the government strictly for current year non-interest expenditure.
• Statement 2 is incorrect because: Effective Revenue Deficit (ERD) equals Revenue Deficit minus Grants-in-Aid for the creation of capital assets, distinguishing consumption expenditure from capital-building transfers to states. (The claim that 'Primary Deficit is calculated by adding Total Revenue Receipts to Gross Fiscal Deficit.' is factually false).
questions.source: Union Budget Documents & Ministry of Finance Glossary

With reference to Fundamental Rights & Constitutional Remedies, consider the following statements:
1. Article 32 guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and was described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the 'very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it'.
2. The writ jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 32 is wider than that of a High Court under Article 226 because it includes ordinary legal rights.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
• Statement 1 is correct: Article 32 guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and was described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the 'very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it'.
• Statement 2 is incorrect because: While the Supreme Court issues writs only for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights under Article 32, High Courts under Article 226 have wider writ jurisdiction extending to both Fundamental Rights and ordinary legal rights ('for any other purpose'). (The claim that 'The writ jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 32 is wider than that of a High Court under Article 226 because it includes ordinary legal rights.' is factually false).
