questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy
questions.question:
Examine the following three statements regarding Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council:
Statement I: Every decision of the GST Council requires a majority of not less than three-fourths (75%) of the weighted votes of the members present and voting, where the Central Government's vote has a weightage of one-third (33.33%) and all State Governments together have a weightage of two-thirds (66.67%).
Statement II: The GST Council is a non-statutory body chaired by the NITI Aayog Vice-Chairperson where the Union Government holds a 51% veto weightage.
Statement III: The GST Council is a constitutional body established under Article 279A (inserted by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016), chaired by the Union Finance Minister with State Finance/Taxation Ministers as members.

Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation:
Statements I and III are correct, whereas Statement II is incorrect.
• Statement I: Every decision of the GST Council requires a majority of not less than three-fourths (75%) of the weighted votes of the members present and voting, where the Central Government's vote has a weightage of one-third (33.33%) and all State Governments together have a weightage of two-thirds (66.67%).
• Statement III: The GST Council is a constitutional body established under Article 279A (inserted by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016), chaired by the Union Finance Minister with State Finance/Taxation Ministers as members.
• Statement II is a distractor and is factually wrong.
questions.source: GST Council Secretariat & PIB Ministry of Finance

With reference to Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM), consider the following statements:

2. Primary Deficit is calculated by adding Total Revenue Receipts to Gross Fiscal Deficit.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
• Statement 1 is correct: Primary Deficit is defined as Fiscal Deficit minus Interest Payments on previous borrowings, indicating the borrowing requirement of the government strictly for current year non-interest expenditure.

2. The Monetary Policy Committee consists of 10 members chaired by the Union Finance Secretary and targets Wholesale Price Index (WPI) inflation at 2%.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
• Statement 1 is correct: Under Section 45ZB of the amended RBI Act, 1934, the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is a six-member statutory body (3 from RBI including the Governor as ex-officio Chairperson, and 3 external members appointed by the Central Government) tasked with maintaining price stability while keeping in mind the objective of growth.

questions.explanation:
Only Statement 1 is correct.

questions.question:
Match List-I (Five-Year Plan / Economic Policy) with List-II (Core Strategy / Growth Model) as tested in APPSC Group-I & Group-II Economy papers:
List-I:
A. First Five-Year Plan (1951–56)
B. Second Five-Year Plan (1956–61)
C. Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974–79)
D. Eleventh Five-Year Plan (2007–12)

List-II:
1. Harrod-Domar Model (Agriculture & Irrigation priority)
2. P.C. Mahalanobis Four-Sector Model (Rapid Heavy Industrialization)
3. D.D. Dhar Model ('Garibi Hatao' / Poverty Alleviation & Minimum Needs)
4. 'Faster and More Inclusive Growth'

questions.explanation:
Correct Match is A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4:
• First Plan (1951–56) was based on the Harrod-Domar growth model focusing on agriculture, price stability, and multipurpose river valley projects.
• Second Plan (1956–61) was architected by P.C. Mahalanobis emphasizing capital goods and heavy industries (Bhilai, Durgapur, Rourkela steel plants).
• Fifth Plan (1974–79) drafted by D.D. Dhar focused on poverty removal (Garibi Hatao) and self-reliance.
• Eleventh Plan (2007–12) had the theme 'Faster and More Inclusive Growth', followed by the Twelfth Plan ('Faster, More Inclusive and Sustainable Growth').

With reference to 73rd & 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts (1992), consider the following statements:
1. The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 added Part IX ('The Panchayats', Articles 243 to 243-O) and the Eleventh Schedule containing 29 functional items to the Constitution.
2. The 73rd Amendment Act added the Twelfth Schedule with 18 items and placed Panchayat elections under the direct supervision of the Election Commission of India (Article 324).

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:

With reference to Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) & RBI, consider the following statements:
1. Under Section 45ZB of the amended RBI Act, 1934, the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is a six-member statutory body (3 from RBI including the Governor as ex-officio Chairperson, and 3 external members appointed by the Central Government) tasked with maintaining price stability while keeping in mind the objective of growth.
2. The Monetary Policy Committee consists of 10 members chaired by the Union Finance Secretary and targets Wholesale Price Index (WPI) inflation at 2%.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
• Statement 1 is correct: Under Section 45ZB of the amended RBI Act, 1934, the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is a six-member statutory body (3 from RBI including the Governor as ex-officio Chairperson, and 3 external members appointed by the Central Government) tasked with maintaining price stability while keeping in mind the objective of growth.
• Statement 2 is incorrect because: The flexible inflation targeting framework mandates maintaining Consumer Price Index (CPI-Combined) inflation at 4% with a tolerance band of +/- 2% (i.e., 2% to 6%). The RBI Governor holds a casting vote in case of a tie. (The claim that 'The Monetary Policy Committee consists of 10 members chaired by the Union Finance Secretary and targets Wholesale Price Index (WPI) inflation at 2%.' is factually false).
questions.source: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Official Portal & PIB Finance Releases

questions.topic: Rivers & Tributaries of Andhra Pradesh (APPSC Group-I & II 2024 PYQ)
questions.question:
Consider the following pairs of Rivers flowing through Andhra Pradesh and their Tributaries:
1. Godavari — Sabari and Indravati
2. Krishna — Tungabhadra, Musi and Munneru
3. Penna (Pennar) — Jayamangali, Kunderu, Sagileru, Chitravati and Papagni
4. Vamsadhara — Mahendratanaya

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation:
All four pairs (1, 2, 3 and 4) are correctly matched.
• Sabari (joining at Kunavaram) and Indravati are major left-bank tributaries of the Godavari.
• Tungabhadra, Bhima, Musi, and Munneru are key tributaries of the Krishna River.
• The Penna River (originating in Nandi Hills, Karnataka and draining into Bay of Bengal at Utukuru, Nellore) has Left-bank tributaries Jayamangali, Kunderu, and Sagileru, and Right-bank tributaries Chitravati, Papagni, and Cheyyeru.
• Mahendratanaya is a major tributary of the Vamsadhara river in Srikakulam/Parvathipuram Manyam region.
questions.source: APPSC Group-II Screening Test (Feb 2024) & Group-I Prelims (2024) Official PYQ

questions.topic: Vijayanagara Foreign Travellers (APPSC Group-I & II PYQ)
questions.question:
Consider the following pairs of Foreign Travellers to the Vijayanagara Empire and the Rulers whose courts they visited:
1. Niccolo de' Conti — Devaraya I
2. Abdur Razzaq — Devaraya II
3. Domingo Paes — Sri Krishnadevaraya
4. Fernao Nuniz — Achyutadevaraya

How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.explanation:
All four pairs are correctly matched:
• Niccolo de' Conti (Italian) visited Vijayanagara around 1420 CE during the reign of Devaraya I.
• Abdur Razzaq (Persian ambassador of Shah Rukh) visited in 1443 CE during the reign of Devaraya II.
• Domingo Paes and Duarte Barbosa (Portuguese) visited during the reign of Sri Krishnadevaraya (1509–1529 CE).
• Fernao Nuniz (Portuguese horse trader/chronicler) visited during the reign of Achyutadevaraya (1529–1542 CE).
questions.source: APPSC Group-I Prelims (March 2024) & Group-II Screening (Feb 2024) Official PYQ

1. Kubja Vishnuvardhana, brother of Pulakesin II, founded the Eastern Chalukya dynasty of Vengi in 624 CE, initiating nearly five centuries of rule in Coastal Andhra.
2. Nannaya Bhatta completed all eighteen parvas of the Andhra Mahabharata single-handedly during the reign of Kubja Vishnuvardhana.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
• Statement 1 is correct: Kubja Vishnuvardhana, brother of Pulakesin II, founded the Eastern Chalukya dynasty of Vengi in 624 CE, initiating nearly five centuries of rule in Coastal Andhra.
• Statement 2 is incorrect because: Under Rajaraja Narendra (1019–1061 CE) at Rajamahendravaram, Nannaya Bhatta began translating the Sanskrit Mahabharata into Telugu, earning the title 'Adi Kavi' (First Poet), assisted by Narayana Bhatta (mentioned in the Nandampudi Grant). questions.question:
With reference to Governor's Legislative Powers (Articles 200 & 213), consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 200, when a State Bill is presented to the Governor, the Governor may give assent, withhold assent, return the Bill (if it is not a Money Bill) for reconsideration, or reserve the Bill for the consideration of the President.
2. A Governor can return a State Money Bill for reconsideration under Article 200 and promulgate ordinances even when both Houses of the State Legislature are in session.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
• Statement 1 is correct: Under Article 200, when a State Bill is presented to the Governor, the Governor may give assent, withhold assent, return the Bill (if it is not a Money Bill) for reconsideration, or reserve the Bill for the consideration of the President.
• Statement 2 is incorrect because: Under Article 213, the Governor can promulgate Ordinances only when the State Legislature (or either House in a bicameral legislature) is not in session; such ordinances must be approved by the State Legislature within six weeks of its reassembly. (The claim that 'A Governor can return a State Money Bill for reconsideration under Article 200 and promulgate ordinances even when both Houses of the State Legislature are in session.' is factually false).

questions.question:
Match List-I (Five-Year Plan / Economic Policy) with List-II (Core Strategy / Growth Model) as tested in APPSC Group-I & Group-II Economy papers:

A. First Five-Year Plan (1951–56)
B. Second Five-Year Plan (1956–61)
C. Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974–79)
D. Eleventh Five-Year Plan (2007–12)

List-II:
1. Harrod-Domar Model (Agriculture & Irrigation priority)
2. P.C. Mahalanobis Four-Sector Model (Rapid Heavy Industrialization)

questions.explanation:

• Eleventh Plan (2007–12) had the theme 'Faster and More Inclusive Growth', followed by the Twelfth Plan ('Faster, More Inclusive and Sustainable Growth').

questions.question:
Consider the following pairs of Rivers flowing through Andhra Pradesh and their Tributaries:
1. Godavari — Sabari and Indravati
2. Krishna — Tungabhadra, Musi and Munneru
3. Penna (Pennar) — Jayamangali, Kunderu, Sagileru, Chitravati and Papagni
4. Vamsadhara — Mahendratanaya

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation:
All four pairs (1, 2, 3 and 4) are correctly matched.
• Sabari (joining at Kunavaram) and Indravati are major left-bank tributaries of the Godavari.
• Tungabhadra, Bhima, Musi, and Munneru are key tributaries of the Krishna River.
• The Penna River (originating in Nandi Hills, Karnataka and draining into Bay of Bengal at Utukuru, Nellore) has Left-bank tributaries Jayamangali, Kunderu, and Sagileru, and Right-bank tributaries Chitravati, Papagni, and Cheyyeru.
• Mahendratanaya is a major tributary of the Vamsadhara river in Srikakulam/Parvathipuram Manyam region.

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: Engineer Team A can complete a section of the Polavaram feeder canal in 20 days, and Engineer Team B can complete the same section in 30 days. They work together for 8 days, after which Team A leaves. In how many days will Team B alone finish the remaining work?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• A's 1 day work = 1/20; B's 1 day work = 1/30.
• Combined 1 day work of (A + B) = 1/20 + 1/30 = (3 + 2)/60 = 5/60 = 1/12.
• Work done in 8 days together = 8 × (1/12) = 2/3.
• Remaining work = 1 - 2/3 = 1/3.
• Time taken by B alone to finish 1/3 work = (1/3) / (1/30) = 10 days.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question:
Statements:
1. All Collectors are Civil Servants.
2. All Civil Servants are Public Authorities.
3. Some Public Authorities are Constitutional Functionaries.

Conclusions:
I. All Collectors are Public Authorities.
II. All Constitutional Functionaries are Collectors.

Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step Venn diagram analysis:
• Since All Collectors ⊂ Civil Servants and All Civil Servants ⊂ Public Authorities, by transitivity All Collectors are definitely Public Authorities (Conclusion I follows).
• Conclusion II does not follow because 'Some Public Authorities are Constitutional Functionaries' does not imply all of them are Collectors.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: Pointing to a photograph, Padma said, 'He is the only son of my mother's father.' How is the man in the photograph related to Padma?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step relation deduction:
• 'My mother's father' = Padma's maternal grandfather.
• 'The only son of my maternal grandfather' = Padma's mother's brother = Maternal Uncle.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: Find the missing number in the APPSC analytical series: 7, 15, 31, 63, 127, ?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step pattern:
• Each term follows the rule: (Previous Term × 2) + 1 (or 2^n - 1).
• 7 × 2 + 1 = 15
• 15 × 2 + 1 = 31
• 31 × 2 + 1 = 63
• 63 × 2 + 1 = 127
• 127 × 2 + 1 = 255.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: Under a Self-Help Group (SHG) linkage programme, Rs. 1,44,000 is distributed among three groups P, Q, and R in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. How much more amount does Group R receive than Group P?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Total ratio parts = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 parts.
• Value of 1 part = Rs. 1,44,000 / 12 = Rs. 12,000.
• Difference between Group R (5 parts) and Group P (3 parts) = 5 - 3 = 2 parts.
• Required difference = 2 × Rs. 12,000 = Rs. 24,000.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: In a certain code language, if 'AMARAVATI' is coded by shifting each letter one position forward in the English alphabet as 'BNBSBWBUJ', how will 'POLAVARAM' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step letter shift (+1 rule):
• P(+1)=Q, O(+1)=P, L(+1)=M, A(+1)=B, V(+1)=W, A(+1)=B, R(+1)=S, A(+1)=B, M(+1)=N.
• Hence 'POLAVARAM' becomes 'QPMBWBSBN'.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: The average foodgrain production of 5 mandals in Krishna district is 420 tonnes. If a 6th mandal's production is included, the average increases to 450 tonnes. What is the production of the 6th mandal?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Total production of 5 mandals = 5 × 420 = 2,100 tonnes.
• Total production of 6 mandals = 6 × 450 = 2,700 tonnes.
• Production of 6th mandal = 2,700 - 2,100 = 600 tonnes.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: In a district development project in Andhra Pradesh, 40% of the total fund is allocated to irrigation, 25% of the remaining fund is allocated to rural roads, and the balance of Rs. 90 Crore is allocated to drinking water under Jal Jeevan Mission. What is the total project fund?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Let Total Fund = X.
• Irrigation allocation = 40% of X = 0.40X. Remaining fund = 60% of X = 0.60X.
• Rural roads = 25% of remaining (0.60X) = 0.25 × 0.60X = 0.15X.
• Balance left for drinking water = 0.60X - 0.15X = 0.45X.
• Given 0.45X = Rs. 90 Crore => X = 90 / 0.45 = Rs. 200 Crore.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: A Vande Bharat Express train 240 meters long crosses a telegraph pole in 8 seconds. How long will it take to cross a railway bridge 660 meters long at the same uniform speed?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Speed of the train = Length of train / Time to cross pole = 240 m / 8 s = 30 m/s.
• Total distance to cross the bridge = Length of train + Length of bridge = 240 m + 660 m = 900 m.
• Time required = 900 m / 30 m/s = 30 seconds.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: The average foodgrain production of 5 mandals in Krishna district is 420 tonnes. If a 6th mandal's production is included, the average increases to 450 tonnes. What is the production of the 6th mandal?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Total production of 5 mandals = 5 × 420 = 2,100 tonnes.
• Total production of 6 mandals = 6 × 450 = 2,700 tonnes.
• Production of 6th mandal = 2,700 - 2,100 = 600 tonnes.

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: In a district development project in Andhra Pradesh, 40% of the total fund is allocated to irrigation, 25% of the remaining fund is allocated to rural roads, and the balance of Rs. 90 Crore is allocated to drinking water under Jal Jeevan Mission. What is the total project fund?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Let Total Fund = X.
• Irrigation allocation = 40% of X = 0.40X. Remaining fund = 60% of X = 0.60X.
• Rural roads = 25% of remaining (0.60X) = 0.25 × 0.60X = 0.15X.
• Balance left for drinking water = 0.60X - 0.15X = 0.45X.
• Given 0.45X = Rs. 90 Crore => X = 90 / 0.45 = Rs. 200 Crore.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: A Vande Bharat Express train 240 meters long crosses a telegraph pole in 8 seconds. How long will it take to cross a railway bridge 660 meters long at the same uniform speed?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Speed of the train = Length of train / Time to cross pole = 240 m / 8 s = 30 m/s.
• Total distance to cross the bridge = Length of train + Length of bridge = 240 m + 660 m = 900 m.
• Time required = 900 m / 30 m/s = 30 seconds.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.question: Engineer Team A can complete a section of the Polavaram feeder canal in 20 days, and Engineer Team B can complete the same section in 30 days. They work together for 8 days, after which Team A leaves. In how many days will Team B alone finish the remaining work?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• A's 1 day work = 1/20; B's 1 day work = 1/30.
• Combined 1 day work of (A + B) = 1/20 + 1/30 = (3 + 2)/60 = 5/60 = 1/12.
• Work done in 8 days together = 8 × (1/12) = 2/3.
• Remaining work = 1 - 2/3 = 1/3.
• Time taken by B alone to finish 1/3 work = (1/3) / (1/30) = 10 days.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question:
Statements:
1. All Collectors are Civil Servants.
2. All Civil Servants are Public Authorities.
3. Some Public Authorities are Constitutional Functionaries.

Conclusions:
I. All Collectors are Public Authorities.
II. All Constitutional Functionaries are Collectors.

Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step Venn diagram analysis:
• Since All Collectors ⊂ Civil Servants and All Civil Servants ⊂ Public Authorities, by transitivity All Collectors are definitely Public Authorities (Conclusion I follows).
• Conclusion II does not follow because 'Some Public Authorities are Constitutional Functionaries' does not imply all of them are Collectors.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.question: Pointing to a photograph, Padma said, 'He is the only son of my mother's father.' How is the man in the photograph related to Padma?
questions.explanation:

• 'My mother's father' = Padma's maternal grandfather.

questions.subject: Mental Ability & Reasoning
questions.question: Find the missing number in the APPSC analytical series: 7, 15, 31, 63, 127, ?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step pattern:
• Each term follows the rule: (Previous Term × 2) + 1 (or 2^n - 1).
• 7 × 2 + 1 = 15
• 15 × 2 + 1 = 31
• 31 × 2 + 1 = 63
• 63 × 2 + 1 = 127
• 127 × 2 + 1 = 255.
questions.source: APPSC Prelims CSAT / Mental Ability Official Pattern

questions.question: Under a Self-Help Group (SHG) linkage programme, Rs. 1,44,000 is distributed among three groups P, Q, and R in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. How much more amount does Group R receive than Group P?
questions.explanation:
Step-by-step calculation:
• Total ratio parts = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 parts.
• Value of 1 part = Rs. 1,44,000 / 12 = Rs. 12,000.
• Difference between Group R (5 parts) and Group P (3 parts) = 5 - 3 = 2 parts.
• Required difference = 2 × Rs. 12,000 = Rs. 24,000.

questions.question:
Match List-I (Five-Year Plan / Economic Policy) with List-II (Core Strategy / Growth Model) as tested in APPSC Group-I & Group-II Economy papers:
List-I:
A. First Five-Year Plan (1951–56)
B. Second Five-Year Plan (1956–61)
C. Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974–79)
D. Eleventh Five-Year Plan (2007–12)

List-II:
1. Harrod-Domar Model (Agriculture & Irrigation priority)
2. P.C. Mahalanobis Four-Sector Model (Rapid Heavy Industrialization)
3. D.D. Dhar Model ('Garibi Hatao' / Poverty Alleviation & Minimum Needs)
4. 'Faster and More Inclusive Growth'

Select the correct code:
questions.explanation:
Correct Match is A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4:
• First Plan (1951–56) was based on the Harrod-Domar growth model focusing on agriculture, price stability, and multipurpose river valley projects.
• Second Plan (1956–61) was architected by P.C. Mahalanobis emphasizing capital goods and heavy industries (Bhilai, Durgapur, Rourkela steel plants).
• Fifth Plan (1974–79) drafted by D.D. Dhar focused on poverty removal (Garibi Hatao) and self-reliance.
• Eleventh Plan (2007–12) had the theme 'Faster and More Inclusive Growth', followed by the Twelfth Plan ('Faster, More Inclusive and Sustainable Growth').

questions.topic: Balance of Payments & Foreign Exchange Reserves
questions.question:
With reference to Balance of Payments & Foreign Exchange Reserves, consider the following statements:
1. India's Foreign Exchange Reserves held by the Reserve Bank of India consist of four components: Foreign Currency Assets (FCA - the largest component), Gold reserves, Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) with the IMF, and the Reserve Tranche Position (RTP) in the IMF.
2. Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) inflows and external commercial borrowings are part of the Merchandise Trade balance in the Current Account.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
• Statement 1 is correct: India's Foreign Exchange Reserves held by the Reserve Bank of India consist of four components: Foreign Currency Assets (FCA - the largest component), Gold reserves, Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) with the IMF, and the Reserve Tranche Position (RTP) in the IMF.
• Statement 2 is incorrect because: In the Balance of Payments (BoP), software service exports and private remittances from the Indian diaspora are recorded under the 'Invisibles' (Services and Transfers) sub-account of the Current Account, whereas FDI and FPI inflows are recorded under the Capital/Financial Account. (The claim that 'Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) inflows and external commercial borrowings are part of the Merchandise Trade balance in the Current Account.' is factually false).
questions.source: RBI Handbook of Statistics on the Indian Economy
